title: Quick check: API Routes in the Pages Router

questions.prompt: In the context of “API Routes in the Pages Router” and “Creating API endpoints”, Which statement best describes the Pages Router?
options: A supported routing system used by existing projects, with pages under `pages/` and its own data-fetching conventions.
The same filesystem convention as the App Router in every detail.
A feature removed from all Next.js versions.
questions.answer_key: A supported routing system used by existing projects, with pages under `pages/` and its own data-fetching conventions.
questions.explanation: The Pages Router remains relevant for maintenance, but it uses its own conventions distinct from the App Router.

lesson_context.lesson_title: API Routes in the Pages Router

questions.prompt: While implementing “API Routes in the Pages Router”, How should a Pages Router to App Router migration be approached?
options: Rename every folder at once without testing.
Delete route tests because the folder structure is different.
Mix data-fetching APIs without checking where they are supported.
Migrate incrementally while preserving URLs and behavior and adding regression tests.
questions.answer_key: Migrate incrementally while preserving URLs and behavior and adding regression tests.
questions.explanation: A staged migration with route parity checks reduces risk and makes failures easier to isolate.

lesson_context.lesson_title: API Routes in the Pages Router

questions.prompt: When reviewing “API Routes in the Pages Router”, Which rule helps maintain a legacy codebase?
options: Apply App Router-only APIs in every legacy page automatically.
Keep legacy conventions explicit and check each API against the version and router that use it.
Assume old caching and runtime behavior remain unchanged forever.
questions.answer_key: Keep legacy conventions explicit and check each API against the version and router that use it.
questions.explanation: Legacy maintenance depends on identifying router-specific behavior and verifying it against the installed version.
